blocks.task_summary: Show that lines L and M intersect at a point A and find the position vector of A.
method_path: Set at least two corresponding components of L and M equal to form equations in s and t
Solve two of the equations simultaneously to obtain s=2 (or t=-1)
Verify the solution satisfies the remaining component equation
Substitute s=2 into L or t=-1 into M to obtain position vector A=(5,8,9)
accepted_alternatives: Use t=-1 and verify in remaining component instead of s=2

evidence.basis: M1: attempt to set at least two components of L and M equal; (M1): attempt to solve two equations simultaneously; A1: s=2 OR t=-1; R1: substitute s=2 and t=-1 into remaining component OR recognition that 2nd and 3rd equations are equivalent; A1: position vector of A is (5,8,9)

blocks.task_summary: Verify that lines L and M both lie in the plane P given by r dot (0,2,-1)=7.
method_path: Substitute the parametric equation of L into r dot (0,2,-1)=7 and verify the identity holds for all s
Substitute the parametric equation of M into r dot (0,2,-1)=7 and verify the identity holds for all t
accepted_alternatives: Show direction of each line is perpendicular to the normal (0,2,-1) AND a point on each line satisfies the plane equation
Show both direction vectors are perpendicular to the normal AND a point on either line satisfies the plane equation

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (M1) attempt to substitute at least one line into the plane equation; A1: L substitution yields 7; A1: M substitution yields 7. METHOD 2: (M1) consideration of direction of one line and a point; A1: direction dot normal = 0 and point on line satisfies plane for L; A1: same for M. METHOD 3: (M1) consideration of direction of both lines; A1: both directions dot normal = 0 or cross product yields scalar multiple of normal; A1: a point satisfies plane equation.

blocks.task_summary: (i) Find the position vector of C where the line through B=(-3,12,2) perpendicular to plane P meets P. (ii) Hence find the magnitude of BC.
method_path: Write parametric equation of line through B with direction (0,2,-1): r=(-3,12,2)+lambda(0,2,-1)
Substitute into plane equation r dot (0,2,-1)=7 to obtain 22+5lambda=7
accepted_alternatives: For (ii): recognise BC is parallel to normal vector, BC=lambda * magnitude_of_normal, so |BC|=|lambda|*|(0,2,-1)|=3*sqrt(5)=sqrt(45)

evidence.basis: (c)(i): (A1) position vector of point on line r=(-3,12,2)+lambda(0,2,-1); (M1) substitute into plane equation; (A1) lambda=-3; A1: C=(-3,6,5). (c)(ii): (M1) BC=OC-OB; (M1) distance formula; A1: BC=sqrt(45)=3sqrt(5). METHOD 2 for (ii): (M1) recognition that BC is parallel to normal; (M1) distance formula on normal vector; A1: BC=3*sqrt(5).

blocks.task_summary: Find the reflection of point B=(-3,12,2) in the plane P.
method_path: Recognise that the reflected point B-prime lies on the same perpendicular line with parameter mu=2*lambda=-6
accepted_alternatives: Use OB-prime=OB+2*BC or OB-prime=2*OC-OB to obtain (-3,0,8)

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: (A1) OB-prime=(-3,12,2)+mu(0,2,-1); (M1) recognition that mu=2*lambda=-6 OR BC=CB-prime; A1: OB-prime=(-3,0,8) so coordinates are (-3,0,8). METHOD 2: (A1) BC=CB-prime=(0,-6,3); (M1) OB-prime=OC+CB-prime OR OB-prime=OB+2*BC OR OB-prime=2*OC-OB; A1: OB-prime=(-3,0,8).
